name: avanor
desc: Quick-growing roguelike game with easy ADOM-like UI
why: An ADOM-like roguelike with an old-school feel, a close call on whether it has enough strangeness.

brief.what_it_is: Avanor is a single-player roguelike game, described on its homepage as a "(not so) quick-growing roguelike game with easy ADOM-like user interface" and titled "The Land Of Mystery". The homepage gives no detail on controls, display, or how a run plays out, so those are unknown from this source. Its news section says the world of Avanor is now described by a Lua script in the development version. Source code was released under open source in July 2003, and the project is by Vadim Gaidukevich.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit motivation. Its framing is a roguelike with an interface modelled on ADOM (Ancient Domains of Mystery) that is easy to use.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the mechanism. Its news notes that the 2005 development version moved the description of the world into a Lua script, and that the 2003 release added furniture, traps, special rooms with creatures, and new monsters.
brief.install_notes: The homepage links to a SourceForge download page (http://sourceforge.net/project/showfiles.php?group_id=167087). The 2005 development version was Win32-only and was stated to be not yet playable. Nothing on the homepage covers hardware, runtimes, or first-run configuration. Installing via Homebrew is the formula named 'avanor' with executable 'avanor'.
brief.standout: It is an old-school ADOM-like roguelike that was open-sourced and has a Lua-driven world description in development. Its homepage is candid about its own delays and status.
brief.status: Quiet. The newest news item is dated 5.06.2006 and says the site had been down for two months and that version 0.6.0 'will be available soon'. The latest release mentioned is 0.5.8 (changes list), with no release date given. The development version from 22.09.2005 was dated after almost two years without a release. I found no evidence of a release after 2006.
brief.caveats: The homepage says the 2005 development version was not yet playable and was Win32 only. Version 0.6.0 was promised in 2006 but I saw no sign it shipped. The README did not mention licence terms beyond 'Open Sourced' and the copyright line. The manual and bug list are linked, but I did not follow them. The homepage was reachable, but the README is thin, so details such as controls and gameplay are unknown.
quotes: Avanor is a (not so) quick-growing roguelike game with easy ADOM-like user interface
It is still not playable and only for Win32 platforms.
Avanor is Open Sourced since this week.
fetch_log: https://avanor.sourceforge.net/ — fetched OK; plain-text homepage with news and changes. Manual, bug list, and forum links are named but no URLs were given in the text, so I did not follow them. Stopped at one fetch because the homepage held the substance.
